gen-gf-amita-fs-spline-sans: Soft, hand-drawn friendliness: that is Amita, rounded and easygoing. And Spline Sans backs it up with wide curve openings and strokes of identical weight, which suits snappier bits of text better than long ones.
gen-gf-amita-fs-synonym: Amita is soft, rounded and hand-drawn, friendly enough to carry just a few lines. But Synonym, the sans-serif, does its best work in plain constant strokes with generous curve openings, while Amita keeps the warmth.
gen-gf-amita-outfit: Relaxed and friendly, Amita draws rounded hand-made letters across the top. Outfit, the sans-serif, bends constant-width strokes into curves that stop short of closing, better for short bursts of text.
gen-gf-amita-plus-jakarta-sans: A hand-drawn feel gives Amita its warmth, soft and rounded. Plus Jakarta Sans does the precise work, a monoline sans-serif with curve endings kept well apart, though not built for lengthy blocks of text.
gen-gf-amita-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, its curves turning corners without any pressure swell. And the pair's best quality is how that exactness sits under Amita's soft hand-drawn warmth, good for a couple of lines.
gen-gf-amita-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk draws each glyph as a ribbon of constant width, with counters that breathe, made for quick glances at text. Amita's soft, rounded, hand-drawn letters loosen things up on top.
gen-gf-angkor-fs-paquito: Paquito is confident and approachable, with caps and lowercase close in height. Angkor, commanding and bold, tightens every rounded letter, so the two make a loud-then-friendly pairing that works on a few lines.
gen-gf-anybody-fs-karma: Karma reads trustworthy and classic, with terminals held clear of the stem. What stands out most is Anybody's bold, flared display voice against that quiet modulation, since the two pack their lowercase up near the caps.
gen-gf-anybody-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and approachable, its lowercase tucked close to the caps. Anybody adds a bold, distinctive display voice with gently flared curve ends, and together the two work best on brief bits of text.
gen-gf-architects-daughter-fs-amulya: Graceful and relaxed, Architects Daughter keeps its stroke weight unvarying, with s curves opening wide. Amulya, a contemporary sans-serif with generous curve gaps, tightens up that hand-drawn looseness, and the pair is happiest in modest amounts.
